Applies RPM/load-driven durability damage to the engine wear value this+412 and, when it is exhausted, flags the failure-state slot (value 9). Runs coupled coolant and oil temperature dynamics over the this+7500..7588 block (including overheat sine damping at 373.16 kelvin) and drives a random component-failure/repair state machine over the this+7604..7672 block, clearing the per-component time array and calling sub_41AC50 on the failure object. Called per frame from VehiclePhysicsIntegrationStep; reuses a global random-sample index (dword_8AAE70) and two global random tables.

operations.description: Engine durability gate: when this+412 (durability) is above zero, v2 = this+428 * this+8 (RPM) * |this+7260| is computed and this+412 is reduced by v2 * this+436; if it reaches zero or below, this+412 and this+416 are zeroed and, when the failure-state slot at *(this+7936)+16488 is clear, it is set to 9 (durability-exhausted code). On the surviving path the engine-power sub-struct is written: *(this+468)+172 = this+412 * 0.75 + 1.0 and *(this+468)+180 = 1.0 / that value.
v56 = fabs(this+7260): the absolute value of the per-frame excitation input is taken once and reused by every thermal and damage equation.

Coolant temperature-rate term: v60 = v2*this+7516 + v56*this+7524 + (flt_8AFEF0 + 273.16 - this+7500)*this+7532, mixing the damage term, the excitation and an ambient-temperature term (flt_8AFEF0 is the kelvin/ambient base).
Heat-sink term: v7 = this+7548, boosted by v56*this+7556 when this+7500 exceeds this+7508 - 10.0 (a threshold with 10.0 hysteresis); then v8 = v7 * (this+7500 - this+7564).
Advance coolant temperature: v57 = (v60 - v8) * this+104 (time delta) + this+7500, stored as an 8-byte double over this+7500 (low dword) and this+7504 (high dword).

When the new coolant temperature v57 is not below (and not equal to) the cap this+7508, the excitation contribution v9 = v56*0.5358549222797928 is clamped by the sine factor sin(this+7508 * 3.141592653589793 / (v57+v57)), floored at zero when negative.
Smoothed coolant output: this+7540 = (v9 - this+7540) * this+104 * 4.0 + this+7540 (exponential smoothing with a 4.0 gain).
Engine-model torque moment: v13 = *(this+5616); v14 = *(v13+92)**(v13+116) + *(v13+108)**(v13+68) + *(v13+44)**(v13+100); v15 = v14*0.2 when v14 is non-negative, otherwise v15 = -v14.
Oil-temperature rate: v58 = (v8 + (v15*this+7580 + this+7572) * (flt_8AFEF0 + 273.16 - this+7564)) * this+104 + this+7564, then stored back into this+7564.

Overheat damping: when the oil temperature v58 exceeds 373.16 (boiling point in kelvin), v16 = v56*0.301625 is scaled by sin(1172.316714613567 / (v58+v58)), floored at zero; then this+7588 = (v16 - this+7588) * this+104 * 4.0 + this+7588.

Component failure countdown: when this+7604 is positive, sub_5881F0 is called twice with the constant 2.0 (accumulating a time/heat contribution), then this+7604 = this+7604 - (2.0 * 0.5 + this+7596) * this+104; when this+7604 stays positive the function returns early.
Failure trigger: when the countdown reaches zero, this+7604 and this+7608 are zeroed and the failure-state slot at *(this+7936)+16488 is set to 1 (component-failure code) when currently clear.

Random failure selection setup: v59 is the prior countdown value; when it equals the double-precision smallest normal 2.225073858507201e-308, a no-selection flag v22 is cleared using flt_8AB274[dword_8AAE70]; otherwise v24 = flt_8AAE74[dword_8AAE70] is sampled and the global index dword_8AAE70 is advanced. v23 detects whether all three component fields (this+7652, this+7660, this+7668) are zero.

When v24 < 0.5, v22 set and all components currently zero, a single component is picked: v29 = v24 +/- 0.04 (sign from compare-flag residue), then threshold bands (below 0.3, 0.3-0.4, 0.4-0.5) write the chosen component field (this+7652, this+7660 or this+7668) = flt_8AB274[sample]*0.4 - 0.1, set this+7604 = scaled v29 + 1.0 and this+7596 = flt_8AB274[sample]*0.1 + 0.15, then return.

When v24 >= 0.5 and v22 set, v35 = flt_8AAE74[advancing index] selects a component to reset to exactly 1.0: below 0.4 resets this+7652/this+7656, below 0.65 resets this+7660/this+7664, below 0.9 resets this+7668/this+7672 (each pair written as the low/high dwords of 1.0).

Component repair pass (LABEL_57): the still-zero components are drifted back toward 1.0 by writing 1.0 - flt_8AAE74[sample]*0.3 into them (this+7652, this+7660, this+7668), with flt_8AAE74 indexing advancing the global dword_8AAE70; a 0.2-bounded branch adds sample+0.1 to a zero component.

Per-component time-array reset: this+7596 and this+7600 are zeroed, then for v45 in 0..this+7432-1 the dword at *(this+7420) + 8*v45 + 4 is cleared; finally sub_41AC50(*(this+7936), 0) is called on the failure object.

Long-quiet branch: when this+7604 < -15.4 and this+7596 > 0, this+7596 = this+104*0.002 + this+7596; when it exceeds 0.6 the pair is clamped by writing the literal dwords 858993459 and 1071854387 into this+7596 and this+7600 (matching the init literals).

In-range decay: when this+7604 lies in [-15.4, 0], this+7604 = this+7604 - this+104; on one compare-flag branch all six component dwords (this+7652..this+7672) are zeroed, on another branch (crossing below -10.1 from above) this+7668 and this+7672 are zeroed and this+7652/this+7660 are halved.

functions.name: SolveSuspensionWheelDynamics
functions.summary: Core per-frame vehicle suspension and wheel dynamics solver. Computes per-wheel constraint projections with ConstraintProjectGramSchmidt, evaluates tire spring/damper force curves from an interpolated lookup table, builds a slip-force target from clamped wheel velocity, then runs a time-stepped LCP (linear complementarity problem) solve over a 6x7 constraint matrix (solved via sub_5677B0) for the four wheels and two brake rows. Applies the resolved impulses to the chassis-body force accumulators reached through this+0x15F0 and this+0x141C and to the four chassis-body pointer objects at this+0x3E8, this+0x84C, this+0xCB0 and this+0x1114. a2 is the time remaining for the sub-stepping loop.

operations.description: Per-wheel constraint projection: call ConstraintProjectGramSchmidt on each of the four wheel constraint objects (base this+652, stride 0x464) and store the four projection results in the local accumulator doubles v243..v246.

Compute the slip-force target v247 from the wheel slip velocity at this+0x1E38 and the coefficient double at this+0x1E68 (with its high dword at this+0x1E6C): the velocity is clamped to +-2.0; inside the range the target is velocity times coefficient times -0.5, otherwise it is the negated coefficient.
Select v234 = min(this+0x1C5C, this+0x1CF4); the resulting comparison flags select which of the three tire-curve branches (positive, clamped-negative, clamped-positive) runs next.

Evaluate the suspension force curves: index the two interleaved float curves stored at the table pointer this+0x1CFC by velocity * 0.03125, using sub_5895A2 as the float-to-int truncation helper, linearly interpolate each curve and write the two results to this+0x1D00 and this+0x1D04. Combine them with the timestep at this+0x8 into the total force v248, with sign handling for the three velocity-range branches.

Apply the total longitudinal force (v248+v247) to the chassis body object reached through the pointer at this+0x15F0: scale by the body's three axes (+0x2C/+0x44/+0x5C) and accumulate into the body force accumulator (+0x14C/+0x154/+0x15C).
Compute the brake-force scale v235 = (1.0 - this+0x20) * (1.0 - this+0x18) * this+0x1E58 from the two input terms at this+0x20 and this+0x18 scaled by the coefficient at this+0x1E58.

Build the per-wheel contact-sign table v252[4] from the wheel velocities stored at this+0x348 (stride 0x464): each entry is -1, 0, or +1 from the velocity sign (high dword of the first double at this+0x34C).
Compute v216, the sign comparison of this+0x1C5C against this+0x1E38 (-1/0/+1), used later to decide whether the second brake constraint row is active.

Mode switch on this+0x1E14 (0/1/2) selecting the brake-impulse strategy. Each path forms a wheel-velocity sum (this+0xC10, this+0x1074, this+0x7AC, and wheel velocity this+0x348), calls FloatEpsilonCompare on the velocity product against this+0x1E38, selects the per-index threshold v211 via the index at this+0x1EF0 (with an external velocity-table fallback) and the threshold v225 at this+0x1E70, then updates wheel constraint coefficients v243..v246 using the spring/damper constants at this+0xC28, this+0x108C, this+0x360, this+0x364 and this+0x7C4 and the damping offsets at this+0x1E18, this+0x1E20, this+0x1E28 and this+0x1E30.

LCP solve loop. Zero the 6x7 constraint matrix region (336 bytes). Build the four wheel Jacobian rows from the v252 signs: wheel velocities at this+0x368 (stride 0x464), spring-constant doubles at this+0x360/0x364 and this+0x7C4, wheel-2/3 coefficient doubles at this+0xC28/0xC2C/0xC30 and this+0x108C, v227 = v211 squared, and the brake Jacobian constants at this+0x1E50/0x1E54. Add the second brake row for v216: either a fixed unit row with the brake scale from this+0x1E58 or a computed row from this+0x1E50 and this+0x1C74 with v247/v248. Solve the system with sub_5677B0(v253, 6), then iterate until every unconstrained wheel row (velocity source this+0x368) and the brake threshold (this+0x1E58) converge.

Write per-wheel slip results: for each wheel store the solved value v127 and v128 = |v127| minus the friction limit at this+0x668 into the slip slots at this+0x660 (stride 0x464, high dword this+0x664), zeroing negative values, and accumulate v129 per wheel.

Build the output force deltas: v258 = v264 * this+0x1E50 and v259 = v265 * this+0x1C74; per-wheel contact forces on the body axes from the spring doubles at this+0x360/0x364 (stride 0x464); ratio-limit slots v228..v231 (each -wheelVelocity/delta with a largest-finite-double sentinel when the denominator is zero); step limits v232 and v233 from this+0x1E38 and this+0x1C5C.

Select the minimum integration step v149 = min(a2, v232, v233, v228..v231) and apply it: scale each wheel velocity slot (this+0x348, stride 0x464) and the double slot before it, then update the accumulators this+0x1E38 and this+0x1C5C (copying the high dword via this+0x1E3C into this+0x1C60 when the corresponding row is inactive).
When a partial step was taken (v149 != a2), rescale the output velocities and force terms by v149/a2 and loop again with the remaining time a2 = a2 - v149 (sub-stepping loop).

Apply the resolved impulses to the chassis and wheel bodies through the four chassis pointer fields this+0x3E8, this+0x84C, this+0xCB0 and this+0x1114 (each exposing body rows at +0x1C/+0x34/+0x4C), scaled by the torque factor at this+0x1EA4, and accumulate into the two body-object force accumulators reached via this+0x15F0 and this+0x141C (+0x2C/+0x44/+0x5C read axes, +0x14C/+0x154/+0x15C writes).
Invoked on the frame path from WheelDataCopy (0x004414D0) and PhysicsStepFrame (0x00441600).
Return void after the sub-stepping loop finishes.

functions.name: VehicleActive
functions.summary: Boolean vehicle-active state check. Returns 0 (inactive) when the double threshold at this+0x1DB4 is <= 0.0, the double threshold at this+0x19C is <= 0.0, or the active-flag byte at this+0x1C59 is zero. Otherwise returns 1 when the override-flag byte at this+0x1D0C is non-zero. Otherwise returns (secondary-state byte at *(this+0x1F00)+0x344C non-zero) combined with the condition-code flags from the preceding comparisons. Invoked on the per-frame path by sub_42C440 and Gearbox.

operations.description: If the double threshold at this+0x1DB4 is <= 0.0, the vehicle is inactive (fall to return 0); the comparison constant comes from dbl_59E420
If the double threshold at this+0x19C is <= 0.0, the vehicle is inactive (fall to return 0); the comparison constant comes from dbl_59E430
If the active-flag byte at this+0x1C59 is zero, the vehicle is inactive (fall to return 0)
Early-exit return 0 when any of the two threshold checks or the active-flag check fails
If the override-flag byte at this+0x1D0C is non-zero, return 1 immediately
Return 1 when the override flag is set

Read the secondary-state pointer at this+0x1F00 and dereference offset +0x344C to obtain the secondary state byte; the final result also combines the condition-code flags v3/v4 captured from the preceding comparisons
Final return: (secondary-state byte != 0) AND (v3 | v4), the vehicle-active result
Invoked by sub_42C440 (0042C440) and Gearbox (00443B70)

functions.name: SuspensionVibration
functions.summary: Updates suspension-vibration state each tick. Always sets the active flag this+0x1C59 to 1 and evaluates whether the accumulator this+0x1C5C is below the threshold this+0x1C84. In the trigger mode (a2 nonzero) and when below threshold, copies the source value this+0x1C84 into the accumulator this+0x1C5C and this+0x1C88 into the rate this+0x1C60. In the non-trigger mode and when below threshold, computes a noise-based vibration value from the table flt_8AB274 indexed by the byte counter dword_8AAE70 (incremented), writing this+0x1D10 = noise * this+0x1D20 + this+0x1D28 + this+0x1D18.

operations.description: Evaluate v2 = (this+0x1C5C < this+0x1C84), the accumulator-vs-threshold compare that gates both vibration modes.
Set the active flag this+0x1C59 to 1 unconditionally.
Branch on the trigger argument a2: nonzero selects the source-copy mode, zero selects the noise mode.
In trigger mode with v2 set, copy the vibration source into the running state: this+0x1C5C = this+0x1C84 and this+0x1C60 = this+0x1C88.
In non-trigger mode, proceed to the noise path only when v2 (below threshold) is set.
Read the noise sample v4 = flt_8AB274[(byte)dword_8AAE70] and increment the byte counter dword_8AAE70.
Accumulate the vibration output this+0x1D10 = v4 * this+0x1D20 + this+0x1D28 + this+0x1D18.
Return void; no explicit return value is produced.

functions.name: PhysicsSubComponentDestroy
functions.summary: Destroys and frees up to five physics sub-component pointers: a four-iteration loop over dword pointers starting at this+0x4C (offsets 0x4C, 0x50, 0x54, 0x58), then a single pointer at this+0x5C. Each non-null pointer is recursively destroyed via PhysicsSubComponentDestroy (self-call at 0x00448570), freed with FreeWrapper_7bcf, and set to 0. Returns the last free result (uninitialised when no pointer was non-null).

operations.description: Repeat four times over dword pointer slots starting at this+0x4C (offsets 0x4C, 0x50, 0x54, 0x58), advancing by one dword each iteration.
Guard on the current slot pointer being non-null before destroy/free; null pointers are skipped.
Recursively destroy the current sub-component via PhysicsSubComponentDestroy.
Free the current slot pointer via FreeWrapper_7bcf and store its result.
Clear the current slot pointer to 0 after freeing it.
Guard on the tail pointer at this+0x5C being non-null before destroy/free.
Recursively destroy the tail sub-component via PhysicsSubComponentDestroy.
Free the tail pointer at this+0x5C via FreeWrapper_7bcf and store its result.
Clear the tail pointer field this+0x5C to 0 after freeing it.
Return the result value from the last FreeWrapper_7bcf call (uninitialised if no pointer was non-null).
